messages.subject: Custom scale .. is it possible?
parts:
Dear All,

I have a very unique situation where I want to customize the y axis in a facet_wrap view. It would allow the smaller values to appear in the graph. As an example, I have changed the scale breaks to go 0, 10000, 100000, 20000 etc but would like to have equal spaces between each tick . I have illustrated the desired view in the attached image file. Your help is highly appreciated.

Regards,
Dipanjan

Assuming that that last break value is supposed to be 200000 instead of
20000 (the break points must be monotonically increasing), yes. There
was a detailed discussion about making custom scales not too long ago:

https://groups.google.com/d/topic/ggplot2/7ddCyXGlKiM/discussion

A particularly tricky part of the process is coming up with the
translation and inverse functions. You need a function which maps 0 ->
0, 10000 -> 1, 100000 -> 2, 200000 -> 3 (and 300000 -> 4?). How do you
want to interpolate between these (linear, with a first derivative
discontinuity at 10000?) Then you have to write the inverse function.
From there the previous linked discussion and my blog posts on the
topic should be able to get you through.

http://blog.ggplot2.org/post/25938265813/defining-a-new-transformation-for-ggplot2-scales

http://blog.ggplot2.org/post/29433173749/defining-a-new-transformation-for-ggplot2-scales-part

Be careful with this kind of non-linear scale, though. It may not be
clear to readers of the graph, at first look, that is non-linear.
Perhaps a light horizontal line at the discontinuity would help, or
different background shadings for the different regimes.

--

Oregon Health & Science University
